correctness.rationale: The reciprocal lower bound ||T_Gamma||²≥1/A and single-atom counterexample to the printed A are correct. But the claimed universal attainment by a continuous K-g dual is FALSE: Douglas factorization produces a bounded H→L² operator, not necessarily the analysis operator of a family of pointwise bounded coefficient maps. Rigorous counterexample: set H=l²(N), Omega=N disjoint-union T with counting plus normalized Lebesgue measures, fiber C, c=1/2 and a_n=2^-n. Let g_n be the unit basis function at the nth counting atom, h_n(t)=exp(2*pi*i*n*t), u_n=c*g_n+sqrt(1-c²)*h_n. Then the u_n are orthonormal in L²(Omega). Define Lambda_omega e_n=a_n*u_n(omega), K e_n=a_n e_n. Each Lambda_omega is a bounded functional because (a_n) is square summable, and ||T_Lambda* f||²=||K*f||², so the optimal lower bound is A=1. There EXISTS a genuine continuous dual Gamma with Gamma_omega e_n=g_n(omega)/c (at circle points zero), ||T_Gamma||=1/c, and T_Lambda T_Gamma*=K. For any dual C=T_Gamma*, the equations imply P_span(u_n) C e_n=u_n, so C=J+Q, J e_n=u_n, ran(Q) orthogonal to ran(J), and ||C||²=1+||Q||². Attaining squared norm 1 would force Q=0 and C=J. But at every t in T the coefficients of J e_n(t)=sqrt(1-c²)*exp(2*pi*i*n*t) are not an l² sequence, so no bounded pointwise functional Gamma_t on l² can implement J outside a common null set. Thus NO genuine pointwise bounded continuous dual attains norm²=1/A, although the family has a bona fide dual. The source has no hypothesis ensuring representability of its Douglas reduced solution. Hence its universal attainment assertion, indispensable to the final theorem, is false, while its separate lower bound and scalar correction survive.
residual_risks: This counterexample disproves universal attainment among genuine pointwise bounded continuous K-g dual families; it does not establish whether the unattained infimum equals 1/A.
The discrete direct-sum analog admits a pointwise synthesis realization; the obstruction uses a non-atomic Fourier component.
No claim is made about stronger theorem hypotheses that explicitly assume a pointwise bounded realization of the reduced Douglas solution.
